author: lockRuby
body:
Hello,

        As a history teacher currently working for Armei Meadows Middle, I would like to point out the inconsistencies in one of your levels, Babylonian Gardens. Seemingly a concept for "Destroy the Monument" (I think it is?), it's an inaccurate depiction of what the Babylonian empire was represented as.

        Babylon was initially founded prior (or by the books) to the reignment of Sargon the Great, ruling from 2334-2279 BCE, and sources state with multiple indications that was one of the founders of Babylon himself, along with temples being in stages of development prior. It had a large port town by the Euphrates River, and it ran on to what we know as the Tigris river. It played an early role in developing more of the ancient world, however now the Babylon we know of back then isn't the same (in obvious light), it should be known that such a depicted level could not exist, unless it was in ruins or made in ancient times (which it's 2015). This makes children who are attempting to learn more about Babylonian society mislead, and for such a mere concept to exist, it should not sway the foundations of society today. We should go by what we know, or at least close to it.

        If a merchant gives an agent corn, wool, oil, or any other goods to transport, the agent shall give a receipt for the amount, and compensate the merchant therefor. Then he shall obtain a receipt from the merchant for the money that he gives the merchant. This is in the Code of Hammurabi (article linked in text) which perfectly defines another problem. As there is no sole merchant, there is neither a receipt nor a person to compensate. Other than automatically being given one of the yellow long things called "Golden Carrots", they did not make any developments off of gold being in food, nor would it be determined as edible. Doing so would have been a detriment to their health, and while it may have been shiny and cool, it's not the right type of thing to be looking at when you're developing a society. They had other priorities and focuses. Though the priorities proved failing and Babylon eventually fell apart, it's a shame that this level loads multiple times in a row if necessary.

        One thing I noticed off the back of my mind is that there is quite a high amount of quartz being used to structure the map. I do not believe that in those times, there was a high supply of "quartz" to construct with, and if even, it wouldn't have been an ideal material due to how fragile it may have been.


        As these being three reasonings to discontinue the Babylonian Gardens map, I'd much appreciate it if you could reconsider the implementation. I am directing this to the administrators of the network KyloCode, ViceWatercolour, and MidnightBeats. Shall nothing be done about this mistake, I will forward this to the School Board of Armei and have this server possibly shut down. I require you to oblige with my requests, and as for this, I thank you for reading it. If you have any questions, you may post them below, as I am a history expert.
